title: The gym-owner website jumps around while it loads on a phone
what: On a mid-range phone over slow 4G, Google's speed test scores the gym-owner site's layout movement at 0.265, worse than Google's 'poor' line of 0.25, and it is the lowest-scoring public page (86). The page loads three web fonts in ten weights that swap in after the text is drawn, and the live workout scene at the top changes its text and numbers as soon as it comes on screen, so words and blocks move under the reader's thumb.
expected: The page stays still while it loads (layout movement under 0.1), so an owner can start reading and tapping straight away.
how_often: every first visit on a phone
fix_line: Find the parts that move in the speed report, give them fixed room, and load fewer font weights with matching fallback sizes.

title: The member website's main picture takes 3 seconds to show on slow 4G
what: Google's speed test on a mid-range phone over slow 4G shows the main picture of the member site after 3.0 seconds, above Google's 2.5-second 'good' line. The page first waits for three web font families (including the Hindi one, also for English readers), and the main phone picture is not marked as the first thing to fetch.
expected: The main picture shows within 2.5 seconds on a slow Indian 4G phone.
how_often: every first visit on a phone
fix_line: Mark the main phone picture to load first and trim the font list so it does not hold up the page.

title: The gym invite page shifts after it opens and is the heaviest public page
what: The invite link page a gym shares (/j/ code) moves after it is drawn: the gym's logo is swapped in only once it has downloaded, and the 'Become a member' card appears only after a second question to the server comes back. Google's speed test measures the movement at 0.109, just above the 0.1 'good' line, and the page weighs 491 KiB, the most of all public pages, mostly the gym's full-size logo shown in a small box.
expected: The page keeps room for the logo and the member card from the start, and downloads a logo no bigger than the box shows.
who: new members opening a gym's invite link
fix_line: Reserve space for the late parts of the invite page and serve a small copy of the gym logo.

title: Each visit to a gym's web page asks again whether the gym takes online payment
what: The gym's page details are kept at the edge for a while, but once online joining payment is switched on, every single page view runs the 'can this gym be paid online' check again, with several database reads, before the page is sent. A gym page shared widely will do this work for every visitor, slowing each page and using up the free plan's read allowance.
expected: The online-payment answer is kept for a short time like the rest of the page, so a busy page does not repeat the same reads for every visitor.
how_often: every view while online payment is on
fix_line: Keep the online-payment answer with the cached page details for a minute or so.
